c74object.name: evi.chorus.digital~
c74object.digest: A basic digital Chorus implementation, with multiple stages and saturation
c74object.description:
evi.chorus.digital~ is a 'max define' for the evi_chorus_digital.gendsp gen~ abstraction. Because evi.chorus.digital~ is a 'max define' it also accepts all messages and attributes that a gen~ object does.
An example of a multi stage chorus using evieve primitives. There are many attributes so that the effect can be macroised in different ways for varying types of sound design.

inlet.description: Reset of internal LFO phases is naive and not antialiased.

outlet.description: Left phase LFO output for downstream synchronisation.
Right phase LFO output for downstream synchronisation.

attribute.name: crossover
attribute.description: Crossover frequency in Hz. Below this crossover point (the bass) the audio is mono summed, saturated and added back into the wet output mix. Above this crossover point the audio is chanelled through the chorus effect.

attribute.name: depth
attribute.description: The relative size of the modulation delay. At 0 the chorus delay is 0 ms, at 1, the chorus delay modulates between its extremes, set by @mintime and @maxtime arguments in ms.

attribute.name: drydelay
attribute.description: This controls the delay time at the dry output mix delay of the chorus. This is a very strange effect and can make the sound very sea sickly depending on @drywet.

attribute.name: drywet
attribute.description: The global dry/wet mix of the chorus. 0 is completely dry, 1 is completely wet.

attribute.name: duty
attribute.description: One of four LFO controls (@duty, @shape, @skew, @zeroreset). @duty changes the duty cycle of the LFO triangle shape.

attribute.name: feedback
attribute.description: The global feedback gain. Strongly affected by the @feedbackmix, @feedbackcross and @stages attributes.

attribute.name: feedbackcross
attribute.description: Between 0..1 @feedbackcross crosses over the L/R of the feeback path to R/L. This can be a very useful sounshaping tool, the effect depends on the polarity of @feeback.

attribute.name: feedbackmix
attribute.description: This attribute will drastically change the sound of the @feedback setting, depending on the @stages attribute. Between 0..1 @feedbackmix morphs the tap point of the feedback path. At 0 the feedback is tapped after the very first stage of the chorus processing, at 1 the feedback is tapped at the end of all the stages. This means that at 0, the feedback will be brittle and strong and probably out of control (depending on @feedback), but at 1, the feedback will be much softer and more maleable (depending on how many @stages are selected).

attribute.name: inject
attribute.description: Like @feedbackmix, @inject morphs the tap point of part of the audio path. @inject is much more subtle that @feedbackmix. It mixes in the wet post crossover mix into the feedback chain before the saturation stage @inject 0) or after the saturation stage (@inject 1), therefore modifying the strength of the saturated feedback path.

attribute.name: invert
attribute.description: Inverts the polarity of the chorussed audio before mixing to the output. Switching invert is smoothed.

attribute.name: maxhz
attribute.description: The maximum in Hz that the @rate attribute can reach. Typically these values are kept small for a chorus.

attribute.name: maxtime
attribute.description: The maximum delay time for the chorus. Whether or not this value is reached depends on the @depth attribute.

attribute.name: mintime
attribute.description: The minimum delay time for the chorus. Whether or not this value is reached depends on the @depth attribute. For a flanger-like effect this is typically 0.

attribute.name: postgain
attribute.description: The gain in dB applied to the wet chain of the processing just before mixing and output.

attribute.name: pregain
attribute.description: The gain applied to the above crossover input before it is sent through the feedback path.

attribute.name: rate
attribute.description: The global speed of the LFO phases. This sets the speed (between 0..@maxhz) the LFOs scale the delay times (set by @depth, @mintime and @maxtime).

attribute.name: shape
attribute.description: One of four LFO controls (@duty, @shape, @skew, @zeroreset). @shape smoothly morphs the LFO shape between triangle (0) and sine (1).

attribute.name: skew
attribute.description: One of four LFO controls (@duty, @shape, @skew, @zeroreset). @skew exponentially shapes the LFO output.

attribute.name: smooth
attribute.description: Smoothing time of the internal parameters.

attribute.name: spread
attribute.description: The left/right spread of the audio outputs, actually the phase offset of the two internal LFOs. 0..1 is exponentially mapped to 0..180 degrees shift.

attribute.name: stages
attribute.description: Sets how many delay stages in serial to use for the chorus. The chorus is created by putting modulated delay lines in a cascade. The more stages, the more delay lines are cascaded are therefore the stronger the chorus effect. Modify the offset of the modulation LFOs per stage with the @warp attribute.

attribute.name: tone
attribute.description: @tone controls a lowpass filter on the input to the feedback path. Lower values will make the feedback recirculation darker, higher value will make it brighter.

attribute.name: warp
attribute.description: The greater the number of @stages the more effect the @warp attribute will have. @warp exponentially shifts the offsets of the LFOs as they cascade down the serial stages of delays.

attribute.name: zeroreset
attribute.description: One of four LFO controls (@duty, @shape, @skew, @zeroreset). If on, changes to the speed (@rate) of the internal LFOs are synchronised to zero reset of phase, which can produce seemless updating of speed changes. Otherwise the speed (@rate) updates smoothly morphing changes.
